bofa.subject: AMZN US: Amazon.com: Price Objective Change - Cloud growth is lumpy, but still quite good; Buy - BUY - United States
bofa.reviewed_text:

---  
Amazon.com  
---  
Cloud growth is lumpy, but still quite good;
Buy  
---  
| | Reiterate Rating: BUY  
---  
PO:317.00 USD   |   Price:243.79 USD  
| Equity   |   30 October 2026  
---  
---  
---  
---  
Key takeaways  
---  
  
  * 3Q rev/EBIT at $201.9bn/$28.1bn mixed vs Street at $202.3bn/$26.1bn. AWS accel'd 2ppts to 39% but missed upside expectations.
  * Mgmt. guided AWS to 40%+ growth in 2027 and 2028, supported by 189% y/y backlog growth to $578bn.
  * We raise '27E EPS by 4% on higher AWS estimates. We trim our PO to $317 and reiterate Buy given strong AI positioning.

  
---  
| FULL REPORT|     |   
---|---|---  
  
* * *  
  
---  
  
AWS revenues fail to impress, but trend is positive

3Q revenues of $201.9bn were close to Street at $202.3bn, while GAAP profit of
$28.1bn beat Street at $26.1bn. AWS growth at 39% accelerated 2ppts q/q, above
Street at 38% (though we think investors were as high as 42%). AI demand
continues to exceed supply, but q/q dollar growth slowed to $3.8bn (below last
quarter at $4.6bn and Cloud peers), suggesting that capacity limitations or
client price adjustments impacted 3Q. 4Q sales guide at $240bn-$247bn and EBIT
guide at $28.5bn-$33.5bn bracketed the Street at $244.6bn and $32.9bn,
respectively.

Building toward a $1 trillion high-margin AWS opportunity

Mgmt. guided AWS to grow 40%+ in both 2027 & 2028, and backlog grew a strong
$82bn q/q to $578bn, which should help investors look past slowing q/q dollar
growth. AWS margins remained strong in 3Q at 39% despite growing depr expense,
and revenue commitments for Graviton and Trainium have each increased more
than 20x year-over-year, which gives us confidence in margin sustainability.
Finally, Amazon indicated plans to sell Trainium chips in 2H'27 which should
provide strong incremental growth in 2028.

4Q guide in-line; raising '27E EPS 4% on higher AWS ests.

We expect AWS to continue to accelerate, and we are at the high end of the
revenue guide, raising revs by $400mn to $246.2bn, but maintaining our EBIT at
$33.5bn (Leo capitalization pushed back to 1Q'27). Given capacity and backlog
growth, we raise AWS estimates and now expect '27E Rev/Profit/GAAP EPS at
$968bn/$145bn/$10.60, up from $961bn/$140bn/$10.24. We raise 2027E capex to
$310bn, up from $302bn.

Remains a top AI play; PO to $317

With strong q/q and y/y backlog growth driven by new enterprise contracts,
steady gains in custom silicon usage & chip sales coming, and Alexa for
Shopping growing usage, we think Amazon has strong AI positioning, the top
theme in tech. Given recent AI sector multiple compression, we trim our sum-
of-parts PO to $317 (from $320) as higher expected AWS revenue growth is
offset by a lower 2027E sales multiple of 8x (from 9x). Our PO implies a 30x
'27 GAAP EPS multiple, well within Amazon's historical valuation range. The
next catalyst is the re:Invent conference, which will likely feature new
Trainium chips, AI applications and, possibly, frontier model progress.

jpm.subject: JPM ANMUTH - Amazon.com: Almost Can’t Help But Buy Amazon
jpm.reviewed_text:
| |  | North America Equity Research  
---|---  
  
# Amazon.com

## Almost Can’t Help But Buy Amazon

  
---  
  
By Doug Anmuth
AC,
Neeraj S Kookada,
CFA,
Daniel
Pfeiffer

Click here for the full document and
disclaimers

| Overweight  
---  
AMZN, AMZN US  
Price (29 Oct 26):$243.79  
Price Target (Dec-27):$365.00  
|   
---  
  
Amazon delivered a solid overall quarter with AI returns increasingly evident,
and management remains bullish on future AWS growth. AWS accelerated to +39%
growth (a $184B revenue run rate), slightly below our +41% estimate, but still
the fastest growth in 5 years, while remaining capacity constrained.
Importantly, AMZN believes AWS can grow above 40% in both 2027 & 2028, &
become a $1T revenue business in the next 5-10 years, w/Stores also possibly
reaching the $1T mark in the same timeframe. Backlog reached $578B, increasing
189% Y/Y & 17% Q/Q, & AMZN has recently emphasized that AWS is sold out
through a good chunk of 2028, while always leaving a certain amount of
capacity for spot/on-demand. We believe management's strong visibility into
demand gives it the confidence to underwrite 40%+ growth over the next 2 years
& to invest even more aggressively in AI compute infrastructure. AMZN left its
outlook for ~$220B in capex in 2026 unchanged, despite outsized spend in 3Q
($77B), but expects to invest meaningfully more in 2027. AMZN also emphasized
that AI is a once-in-a lifetime opportunity—the biggest transformation in our
lifetime—and that it is going to continue to invest to be the leader in
infrastructure & AI. Accordingly, we do not expect any slowdown in capex, and
we're raising our already Street-high estimate for 2027 from $366B to $395B
(+77%). That pushes AMZN to more materially negative FCF at an estimate of
-($128B) in 2027, but AMZN continues to have servers & networking payback in
less than 3 years w/a useful life of 5-6 years, & data centers have 30 year
useful lives and see 5-6 generations of chips. Access to capital will remain
top of mind for investors & we expect AMZN to primarily fund capex through
operating cash flow, the debt market, & leasing opportunities. We recognize
there will likely be some pushback on increasing investments & greater FCF
burn in the near-term, but AMZN is showing the returns & building for a much
bigger business in the medium to long-term. We reiterate our Overweight rating
& our $365 PT is based on 26.5x 2028E GAAP EPS of $13.82.

KEY THOUGHTS AFTER CALLS WITH MANAGEMENT

  * AWS Acceleration Continues, But Short of High Expectations. AWS revenue accelerated to ~39% growth (vs. 37% in 2Q), the fastest growth in ~5 years, but was short of buyside expectations of ~42%. Despite the expectations miss in 3Q, bigger picture, Amazon now expects AWS to reach revenue of $1T in the next 5-10 years (vs. $184B run-rate in 3Q) and expects growth of 40%+ in each 2027/2028 (vs. consensus of 35%/30%). AWS Backlog increased by $82B (+17% Q/Q) to $578B, surpassing GOOGL’s 3Q-ending $561B. AWS continues to see momentum in AI, w/AWS’s AI business growing triple-digits Y/Y in 3Q, driven in part by strong Bedrock growth, with Fortune 500 companies spending ~7x more Y/Y and total Bedrock token volume growing ~17x Y/Y. Amazon believes that over time Bedrock could reach the size of its EC2 business. The chips business also continued to grow triple-digits Y/Y in 3Q, with revenue commitments for Graviton and Trainium each increasing more than ~20x Y/Y. Amazon also announced it intends to begin selling Trainium chips externally in late 2027, which is expected to realize more revenue in the short-term relative to selling intelligence & inference through AWS instances.Core AWS compute/storage revenue grew at its fastest rate in several years, with Amazon seeing a strong linkage between core services and AI spend as more AI workloads move into production and drive additional demand for compute, storage, and networking. AWS continues to make progress on margin expansion despite the drag from AI revenue, with margin expansion of ~400bps to 38.7%. However, we note that margin expansion going forward may not be linear with lower margin AI revenue increasing as a % of the mix, and higher component pricing beginning to flow through the P&L in the form of depreciation. We run AWS margins in the high-30s% range going forward.
  * 2026 Capex Outlook Maintained, But We Expect Continued Heavy Multi-Year Ramp. Amazon maintained its 2026 capex outlook of $220B (+71% Y/Y) despite 3Q capex of $77B coming in 31% higher vs consensus, however, we believe the heavier 3Q spend was a function of timing. Amazon highlighted that it continues to accelerate its capex payback and that there is a clear line-of-sight to attractive financial returns. As such, Amazon indicated that it expects to spend “meaningfully more” on capex in 2027, which is likely why it provided an AWS outlook for the next 2 years. We do not expect capex growth to decelerate or slow next year, and as such we project capex of $395B in 2027 (+77% Y/Y) followed by $476B in 2028 (+20% Y/Y).
  * Solid Stores Growth, But Ads Impacting 4Q OI. Stores growth (1P+3P) of 2.5% FXN was in-line with our expectations w/unit growth of 12%, and everyday essentials now represent ~half of all units globally. We note that Prime Day occurred in 2Q for most of Amazon’s largest countries, including the U.S., which drove the deceleration in growth from 15.4% FXN in 2Q, and was a 400bps headwind to total revenue growth in 3Q. Prime Day also impacted Ads Revenue growth by 850bps which decelerated from 26% FXN in 2Q to 12% FXN Y/Y in 3Q. Additionally, Ads growth was impacted by timing with the lack of NBA on Prime in 3Q and lapping SEM programs that drove greater monetization in 3Q25. That being said, Amazon expects Ads growth to reaccelerate to a high-teens % in 4Q, albeit still below recent growth levels of 20%+. Moving to profit, Amazon guided to 4Q OI of $28.5B to $33.5B, which was lower than investor expectations and our estimate at the midpoint. The outlook was impacted by ~$1B from the delay of Project Leo capitalization, along w/slower Ads growth and increases to fuel and line haul inflation. 
  * Other Notable Points. 1) Amazon is on track to reduce cost to serve per unit for the 4th consecutive year while increasing speed, which is fueling the grocery business reaching $250B TTM gross sales; 2) Management highlighted that agentic shopping from external agents is not impacting Amazon Ads and that few customers are shopping with agents as the experience is still not better or more convenient than coming directly to a retailer; 3) Prime Video has reached a revenue run-rate in the tens of billions of dollars and is now profitable in its own right.

---  
---

---  
Key takeaways  
---  
  
  * D/g to Neutral from Buy, lower PO to $100 from $145, given agentic server CPU tide is more than offset by PC/supply headwinds
  * External foundry progress still TBD, we lower N-T CY27/28E EPS by -16%/-4%. Now see CY30E EPS power of $5-$6 vs. $6-$7 prior
  * Read across positive for AI data center and semicaps (incremental capex), though AMD mixed on PC headwind vs. Helios/MI ramp

  
---  
| FULL REPORT|     |   
---|---|---  
  
* * *  
  
---  
  
Agentic tide more than offset by PC/supply headwinds

We downgrade INTC to Neutral from Buy. In our view, the stock has not
communicated enough traction with external foundry customers, while its data
center strength is offset by a surprisingly sharp drop in PC shipments (down
25-30% QoQ in Q4, further inventory correction expected in 1H27). Data center
CPU is doing well in a rising agentic tide, but faces a tight supply
(substrate) environment, and products are not yet technically competitive
against AMD/ARM-based rivals that are growing 2x-4x faster. On the positive
side, we acknowledge INTC's longer-term ability to develop a competitive
domestic foundry with any signs of traction potentially driving a recovery in
a relatively under-owned stock.

Lower CY30 EPS power to $5-$6 from $6-$7 prior

Overall, we lower CY27/28E EPS by -16%/-4% to $1.69/$2.79. Our longer-term EPS
model forecasts foundry wins becoming more prominent in CY28-30, driving EPS
power towards $5.89, on which we apply a ~20x PE multiple, discounted back to
CY28 to get to our $100 PO (down from $145 based on ~29x prior CY30 EPS power
of $6.14). Our new $100 PO conceptually implies a $550bn market cap, made of:
1) $450bn in Products (roughly half of AMD market cap which comprises an
overlapping server CPU, but a distinct GPU business), and 2) remaining ~$100bn
in the emerging Foundry which could inflate as/when INTC announces external
customer traction on 18A-P/14A. Best-in-class foundry TSMC trades ~11x P/S, so
a $100bn implied valuation suggests an implicit $8-10bn in external business
(of which can eventually expand to 8-10% of overall wafer foundry TAM of
~$380bn as a US-based second or third source supplier).

Read-across: positive AI/semicaps, incr. negative AMD

PC weakness is likely to weigh on rival AMD (up to $750mn PC headwind, offset
by $500mn+ strong server CPU revenue), which reports next week, with consensus
calling for client PC flat into Q4 vs. INTC down 25-30%. However, AMD
Helios/MI ramp could be a strong positive offset. INTC data center strength is
positive for AI semis NVDA, AVGO, MRVL, while spending intentions (CY27
growth, with a rising mix of equipment spend) are a positive for semicaps,
especially KLAC, lithography, AMAT, LRCX.



  

| | Vivek Arya    
Research Analyst

# Intel

## DCAI Growth to Be Crimped Again in CY27 on Supply Chain Challenges; PC
Resetting Lower Through 1H27; Lowering Estimates and PT

  
---  
  
By Harlan Sur
AC,
Mayur
Ramdhani,
Apoorva
Kumar,
Akanksh
Chauhan

Click here for the full document and
disclaimers

| Neutral  
---  
INTC, INTC US  
Price (29 Oct 26):$92.07  
**▼** Price Target (Dec-27):$80.00  
Prior (Dec-27):$85.00  
  
INTC delivered a decisive Sep-Q beat (off strong DCAI growth + continued GM
expansion), but the Dec-Q guide reflects deeper-than-expected PC weakness,
compounded by ongoing supply challenges and the temporary shutdown of Fab 28
in Israel, which in sum drive our forward estimates and PT lower even as the
longer-term DCAI/foundry story remains constructive: (1) Sep-Q results came in
ahead of Street, with DCAI growing +78% Y/Y on broad hyperscale, enterprise,
and neocloud strength, and INTC’s ASIC business more than doubling Y/Y (to a
~$2.8B run-rate per JPMe), underscoring mgmt’s execution turnaround and
reinforcing INTC’s server CPU franchise as a key bull-case lever; (2) Dec-Q
revenue guidance came in below Street, with CCPG likely tracking >20% lower
Q/Q, against a declining PC TAM in CY26 (mgmt sees the unit TAM -12% in CY26
and -10% in CY27, broadly consistent with JPMe), an inventory correction
extending through at least 1Q27, and the Israel Fab 28 shutdown contributing
~$300M of Q4 revenue impact (and a similar impact likely in Q1); (3) GM
guidance of 38% is well below the Street bar, with the ~600bps Q/Q decline
driven roughly equally by lower volume, mix, and Israel impact, though we
would note the Israel ~200bps scrap drag is Q4-concentrated and should largely
roll off, setting up Q1 GM back toward ~40% and FY27 GM expansion consistent
with mgmt’s 40-60% fall-through framework; (4) the forward investment cycle is
stepping up materially, with CY27 capex to grow “strongly” from the $20B CY26
baseline (JPMe ~$26B), CY27 FCF confirmed negative, Fab 62 Arizona + Ohio
accelerating, and the $23B August equity offering explicitly positioned to
fund this trajectory; (5) foundry execution continues to improve - Intel 18A
costs down ~40% since Q1 with yields ahead of plan, 14A 0.9 PDK released on
schedule in October, 18A-P on track for year-end launch with “a couple of
highly strategic customer” engagements, and 10+ CPU LTAs now signed (incl.
publicly-disclosed Oracle). Net, DCAI acceleration and foundry progress
strengthen the LT story but near-term PC softness, Israel drag, and a
negative-FCF CY27 drive estimate revisions lower, with risk/reward remaining
balanced at current levels. We lower our estimates and reduce our Dec-27 PT to
$80 (from $85). We maintain our Neutral rating on INTC.

  * Solid Sep-Q results led by strongest DCAI growth in 15 years; GM expansion driven by Intel 3 / 18A cost declines and favorable mix. Sep-Qtr revenue of $16.5B (+21% Y/Y) landed in line with Street. DCAI revenue grew to $7.3B (+17% Q/Q, +78% Y/Y - the strongest sequential growth for the segment in 15 years), driven by broad-based momentum across hyperscale, enterprise, and neocloud customers plus ASIC growing >50% Q/Q and more than doubling Y/Y. CCPG revenue of $8.1B declined -9% Q/Q and -5% Y/Y as memory shortages pressured TAM, though Intel 18A client CPUs now represent ~1/3 of client revenue (vs. <5% in Q1). Intel Foundry revenue of $6.7B (+58% Y/Y) grew on better-than-expected Intel 3 + Intel 18A output, with the segment operating loss narrowing to -$1.9B (vs. -$2.3B Y/Y) on Intel 3 costs down ~15% since Q1 and Intel 18A costs down ~40% since Q1 (both ahead of plan) while external foundry revenue grew to $411M (+$118M Q/Q, primarily driven by a non-recurring customer program). GM of 44.1% was ~200bps ahead of Street, driven by cost improvements on Intel 3 and 18A plus favorable product mix. EPS of $0.52 landed well above $0.40 Street, with operating leverage flowing through. 
  * Dec-Q guide reflects acute PC weakness and the Israel Fab 28 impact; CY27 capex stepping up materially with FCF confirmed negative. Dec-Q revenue guidance of $15.0-16.0B (midpt $15.5B, down ~6% Q/Q) came in below Street (~$17.0B), with CCPG guided down >20% Q/Q as PC TAM is now forecast at -12% in CY26 and -10% in CY27 (vs. prior less-acute framing), with OEM inventory correction extending through at least 1Q27 as customers aggressively reduce weeks of inventory. DCAI is expected to grow mid-teens% Q/Q (with ASIC revenue growing faster than DCAI overall), partially offsetting the CCPG headwind. The Israel Fab 28 shutdown (factory reopening by end of this week) is embedded in the guide at ~$300M of revenue impact and ~200bps of GM impact (concentrated in 10nm server products), with a similar $300M revenue impact likely in Q1 (though scrapping largely rolls off). GM was guided down ~610bps Q/Q to 38.0%, with the decline driven roughly equally by lower volume on fixed costs, mix, and Israel impact. CY27 capex guided to be up “strongly” from the $20B FY26 baseline (we think $26B+ is reasonable), with firm equipment PO’s +40% Q/Q, Fab 62 Arizona accelerating, and Ohio exploring further acceleration, translating to negative FCF for CY27 (per our estimates).

jpm.reviewed_text:

---|---  
  
# Sandisk

## Strong Results and Guidance; DC Mix Rising; NBM Targets Unchanged, but
Customer Discussions and Pipeline Remain Encouraging; Reit OW

  
---  
  
By Harlan Sur
AC,
Apoorva
Kumar,
Akanksh
Chauhan,
Mayur
Ramdhani

Click here for the full document and
disclaimers

| Overweight  
---  
SNDK, SNDK US  
Price (29 Oct 26):$1,330.05  
Price Target (Dec-27):$2,250.00  
  
Sandisk Corporation (SNDK) posted a strong set of F1Q results and an F2Q guide
that came in modestly ahead of Street estimates. Datacenter demand continued
to accelerate as SNDK allocated more supply to enterprise SSDs, but unlike
last quarter, higher bit shipment volumes drove most (~60%) of the sequential
revenue growth, with pricing contributing the remaining ~40% (based on our
math, this would imply ASP growth of ~9-10% Q/Q and bit volume growth of ~13%
Q/Q). That compares with pricing accounting for ~66% of sequential growth last
quarter, making this print a stronger signal of underlying customer demand
rather than simply another ASP-led quarter. At the midpoint, the F2Q guide
calls for revenue of $12.4B, up ~12% Q/Q, while non-GAAP GM is expected to
hold near 85%, implying continued growth without a material step-down in
profitability. From an end-market perspective, DC remains the clear growth
engine for the company (~44% of revs, with mix to keep rising) and management
expects DC bit demand to grow ~40% Y/Y in CY27 (after more than doubling in
CY26), with the segment representing 55%+ of industry NAND bits in CY27. As
for NBMs (new business model agreements), SNDK surprisingly left its
quantitative guidance from last quarter unchanged, with the company continuing
to expect ~50% of its FY27 bits and ~66% of its FY28 bits as committed under
NBMs. That said, management did clarify that the 2 NBMs closed during F1Q had
already been announced on last quarter’s call, and hence they did not
represent incremental wins for this update. Nonetheless, management’s
qualitative commentary on the NBM pipeline was encouraging, with the team
citing discussions with existing customers about extensions and additional
commitments, alongside interest from new customers. Note that management did
softly indicate that it expects the portion of bits committed under NBMs in
FY28 to move a bit higher over the coming months / quarters (implies 66%+ of
FY28 bits under NBMs). The team also interestingly noted that demand from its
current NBM pipeline exceeds its available supply through the end of the
decade, and so all in, we read the lack of an explicit quantitative update as
a function of SNDK being selective about how it allocates supply, rather than
any sign of weakening customer interest. All in, we view tonight’s results as
further evidence that rising DC mix and longer-duration customer agreements
can support more durable earnings power, with new products like HBF (first
tapeout in F1Q with product samples targeted for CY27) continuing to represent
potential upside to the company’s LT model.

  * Strong F1Q results led by accelerating DC demand and stronger bit shipments… SNDK reported revenues of $11.03B (+23% Q/Q, +378% Y/Y), exceeding the top-end of the guided range ($10.3 -10.8B) and Street expectations (~$10.69B). Roughly ~60% of the sequential increase in revenues this quarter came from volume (bit shipment) growth, with the remaining ~40% coming from pricing, marking a reversal from the prior quarter, where pricing drove most of the increase. DC revenues grew to $4.80B (+61% Q/Q) as SNDK allocated more bits to the segment. Edge revenues grew to $5.83B (+7% Q/Q) supported by growth across automotive and IoT customers. Consumer, on the other hand, declined to $397M (-29% Q/Q) as customers adjusted to higher pricing. As for other financial metrics, non-GAAP GMs rose to 85.1% (up from 84.6% last quarter) while non-GAAP EPS marched higher to $49.51, well above Street estimates (~$46.36).

  * F2Q guide stronger than expected, with continued positive sequential growth and GMs sustaining in the ~85% range… At the midpoint, SNDK guided F2Q revenues to $12.4B (+12% Q/Q), modestly ahead of Street estimates (~$12.1B) but a touch light relative to the buyside estimates we had heard coming into the print. Non-GAAP GMs were guided to 84.5%–85.5%, which embeds modest like-for-like price increases as per management. The board of directors has also approved an 8-for-1 stock split with additional shares to be distributed on Nov-19-26 and the stock set to begin trading on a split-adjusted basis on Nov-20-26. On a pre-split basis, management guided F2Q non-GAAP EPS to $56.00 at the midpoint, well ahead of Street estimates (~$52.72), reflecting stronger-than-expected sales growth and robust operating leverage. On a split-adjusted basis, non-GAAP EPS is expected to be $6.88-7.13, or ~$7.00 at the midpoint.

  * NBM commitments unchanged, with additional customer discussions ongoing… SNDK kept its outlook for ~50% of FY27 bits and ~66% FY28 bits committed under NBMs unchanged, noting that the 2 agreements closed in F1Q had already been announced on last quarter’s call. That said, existing customers are discussing extensions and additional volumes, alongside interest from new customers, with management indicating that FY28 commitments could move a bit higher from ~66% figure over the coming months. The team also noted that demand in its NBM pipeline exceeds available supply through the end of the decade, making supply allocation between existing and new customers an important consideration. Moreover, management clarified that although NBMs remain DC-centric, SNDK has agreements with Edge customers and is open to extending the model where it makes sense. All in, we view the unchanged figures as more a reflection of SNDK being selective with supply rather than a sign of weaker customer interest, though these discussions still need to translate into additional agreements. 

  * Adjusting estimates and maintaining PT at $2,250… After layering in this quarter’s results and management’s updated outlook, we are raising our forward estimates (off of the higher out-quarter guide) and maintaining our PT at $2,250. Our December 2027 price target assumes SNDK trades at ~9x (in-line with the company’s LT median forward memory P/E) applied to our higher CY27 EPS estimate of $260 (up from $250 prior). Reiterate OW. 



Click here for the full document and
disclaimers

Key takeaways  
---  
  
  * SNDK reported a strong beat on F1Q rev/EPS; F2Q guide maintains momentum; 8 for 1 stock split on Nov. 19.
  * Datacenter revs inc. 61% q/q; NBMs commit 50% of F27 bits and 67% of F28 bits.

Strong beat; F2Q guide extends earnings momentum

SNDK reported F1Q revenue of $11.0 bn and EPS of $49.51, above its guidance
ranges of $10.3bn-10.8bn and $44-46, respectively, with revenue up 23% q/q.
Roughly 60% of the growth came from volume and 40% from pricing. The GM
reached 85.1% vs. 84.6% in F4Q26. F2Q revenue and EPS guidance of $12.2-12.6bn
and $55-57 continues upward while 84.5-85.5% GM guidance remains strong
despite component-cost inflation. SNDK announced Board approval for an 8 for 1
stock split (to be distributed Nov 19th). We take this opportunity to
reiterate our Buy rating on the secular opportunity as AI inference makes NAND
more indispensable, though we lower our target multiple to reflect more late-
cycle valuation concerns, and this brings our PO to $2000 (from $2,500).

DC accelerates and AI demand visibility strengthens

DC revenue rose 61% q/q to $4.8bn, materially outpacing overall growth, as the
company allocated more supply to DC. Edge rose 7% to $5.8bn and Consumer fell
29% to $397mn. Mgmt expects industry DC bit demand to grow 40% y/y in C27
after more than doubling in C26, with DC exceeding 55% of the market.
Importantly, customer demand remains strong and SNDK expects its DC mix to
move higher through C27.

NAND in demand, NBM pipeline exceeds supply

SNDK NBMs cover eight DC/Edge customers, $93.9bn in minimum revenue at floor
pricing, and $88.9bn in RPOs, with ~50% of F27 bits and ~67% of F28 bits
committed. The NBM pipeline now exceeds supply through 2030, existing
customers are evaluating extensions and multiple customers are returning for
additional commitments. Mgmt expects NBM share to rise further while remaining
selective on future counterparties.

Buybacks continue, but cyclical concerns rise; PO to $2000

SNDK repurchased $5.0bn in stock in F1Q, taking the total buyback size over
last 2Q to $9.5bn, leaving $10.5bn available. F1Q cash flow from ops was
$6.4bn, and adjusted FCF was $5.7bn including $465mn of NBM
prepayments/deposits and Flash Venture activity of $148mn; cash ended at
$5.1bn. Capex should rise in dollars in F27 to support BiCS 8/10 to ~5% of
revenue. Our F27E rev/EPS move to $48.9bn/$225 from $52.6bn/$234. Our PO
changes to $2000 on 8x (previously 10x) C27E EPS of $251 (prior $255).

bofa.reviewed_text:

Is consensus mis-modeling the staggered launch and risk to gross
margins?  
---  
| | Reiterate Rating: BUY

PO:370.00 USD   |   Price:348.91 USD  
| Equity   |   30 October 2026  
---  
---

---  
Key takeaways  
---  
  
  * We expect Apple to report a slight beat in Sep but Dec guide will reflect the impact of launch cadence and cost headwinds
  * Our analysis shows GMs are modeled too high by consensus for Dec/March/June and revs too high for Dec, too low for June
  * Reiterate Buy; cautious on near term setup given potential headwinds relative to consensus

  
---  
| FULL REPORT|     |   
---|---|---  
  
* * *  
  
---  
  
Our estimates are below Street heading into earnings

As we head into F4Q26 (Sep Q) earnings after market close on Mon, Nov 2nd,
investor focus will likely be on component cost inflation, durability of GM
and services revenue growth. We have incorporated a more conservative outlook
overall given the staggered launch of iPhones (Pro, ProMax and Duo in Sep and
base model, Air in March) and higher prices in response to component cost
inflation. In our view, consensus is too high for revs in Dec, GMs in March
and too low for revs in the June qtr (but too high for GMs) given the
staggered launch this year. We lower our F27 iPhone est. by 9mn units to 247mn
(vs. St at 260mn). Our F4QE rev/EPS are $113bn/$1.97 vs. St at $114bn/$1.99.
Our F1Q27 rev/EPS are meaningfully below St. but could prove conservative esp.
on gross margins depending on residual tariff refunds and memory inventory. We
view margin pressure as transitory and model higher margins starting end of
F27 into F28. Reiterate Buy.

Services rev pressure: weak App Store, and Google TAC

We model F4Q Services rev growth of 10% y/y, consistent with guidance (similar
y/y growth as last qtr, ex the 2.5%+ FX benefit). In F4Q App Store rev grew
1.8% y/y which is a further slowdown from the 3.8% y/y growth seen in F3Q, and
12.8% y/y growth in F2Q25. Google recently reported lower than expected revs
from Search, which can pressure Apple's Licensing revs and increase investor
concerns related to transition of search traffic to AI formats, and pressure
from competing Agentic offerings.

Modeling gross margins to remain under pressure

In Fig 1, we estimate the overall impact of memory and various offsets through
March qtr. on gross margins. We see a gross 900bps impact from memory on
iPhone GMs which is netted down to a negative impact of 500bps based on price,
mix, and cost actions. We estimate about 250bps negative impact on total
company GM. Sep quarter GM guide is 47-48% which includes 100bps of positive
impact from tariff refunds. Assuming a Sep base GM of 46.5% (ex tariff
impact), by the Mar qtr, we would estimate total company GM to be 43.6-44.6%,
much lower than current St. ests (47.7%).

Tweaking estimates; PO stays at $370

A weaker USD could help estimates in the Sep qtr relative to the 2.5% embedded
in the guide. Our PO is $370 on 35x C28E EPS of $10.79. We roll-over to C28
based valuation.

ms.subject: IDEA: Aixtron SE (AIXGn.DE): More than a Flash of Opto Strength
ms.reviewed_text:
| | | |

---  
| | |   
---  
Aixtron SE (AIXGn.DE)  
More than a Flash of Opto Strength  
| | Read Full Report  
---  
(PDF: 14 Pages)  
---  
| Europe  
---  
Stock Rating   Overweight  
Price Target   €42.00  
Lee Simpson, Shawn Kim, Amelia M Scicluna  
October 30, 2026  
---  
| WHAT'S CHANGED?  
---  
Aixtron SE (AIXGn.DE)  
Rating  
| From:   Equal-weight| To: **Overweight**  
---|---  
Price Target  
| From:   €40.00| To: **€42.00**  
---|---  
| | Aixtron delivered a Q3 print that signalled durable opto strength into 2027. Aixtron's capacity flexibility differentiates it to peers while bright spots are also emerging in power electronics. We upgrade to OW, PT €42.   
---  
| | Key takeaways  
---  
  
  * Opto momentum is broadening, supporting a less seasonal sales profile. We see €865mn FY27 sales, 6% above consensus. 
  * GaN recovery is gaining traction, with improving utilisation and double-digit 300mm tool orders in preparation for 2027 across multiple customers. 
  * Unlike peers, Aixtron faces limited capacity constraints, with Malaysia expansion on track, supporting growth and operational flexibility. 
  * Stronger fundamentals and a 20x FY27 P/E offer an attractive entry point. 
  * Upgrade to OW with a €42 PT, based on 25x FY27 EPS (€1.65). 

  
  
Opto durability confirmed. At the Q3 print, Aixtron reported orders of €250mn,
25% ahead of consensus, with management indicating this is likely to remain
the order run rate for FY27. While opto’s share of equipment order intake
eased slightly to 68% (Q1 70%, Q2 75%), we think the €549mn backlog, mostly
attributable to indium phosphide optical equipment, supports strong revenue
visibility into 2027+. Our EW thesis assumed upside was limited to the near
term and lacked durability. This print gives us greater conviction in a more
sustained opportunity, with demand continuing to broaden and momentum
extending to more laser suppliers globally. We therefore expect a more muted
seasonal growth profile in 2027: against sequential sales declines of 50% in
1Q25 and 68% in 1Q26, we expect a smaller decline in 1Q27. We currently model
1Q27 sales of €189mn, -14% qq but +218% yy. With the backlog strengthening and
orders likely to move higher over the coming quarters, we see at least €800mn
of FY27 sales as achievable. Overall, we forecast FY27 sales of €865mn, +6%
above the street.

Broadening recovery supports meaningful 2027 growth. While optics remained the
focus, emerging traction in power electronics was notable, led by GaN. At
earlier prints this year, management pointed to limited GaN visibility, where
we thought data centre orders were particularly elusive. This quarter,
management struck a more constructive tone. GaN utilisation has normalised,
and customers are planning expansions and new tool purchases, a trend
management expects to continue through 2027. Demand is centred on low- to
medium-voltage devices (20-200V) for AI data centre infrastructure, such as
intermediate bus converters (IBCs), battery backup units (BBUs) and auxiliary
power supplies, while 650V consumer devices are adding only marginally. Signs
were already emerging earlier in the week, with Infineon announcing a high
volume GaN manufacturing facility on 300mm wafers (see our first take
here,
where we flagged a positive read-across to Aixtron). We think commentary on
preparing for double-digit 300mm tool orders for 2027, spanning more than one
customer, points to a meaningful GaN contribution to FY27 sales. That said, we
do not expect a similar growth profile in SiC. STMicroelectronics’ commentary
yesterday suggests that while utilisation at analog companies continues to
improve, SiC demand remains relatively soft. SiC content is also growing in
the data centre, for instance in SSTs, but at a smaller scale than GaN; the
main driver remains electric vehicles. Together, we expect GaN and SiC to
contribute to higher estimates next year.

Capacity flexibility versus peers. This reporting season, many companies
across our global coverage have highlighted constraints limiting growth into
FY27/28. Aixtron flagged hiring difficulties, but we did not hear of the
broader capacity constraints affecting many peers. Instead, management
reiterated that capacity should not restrict growth, with no concerns around
production capacity or clean rooms being full. Importantly, the Malaysia fab
remains on track for 2028, with Aixtron expecting to use the facility from Q3
2027. We think this capacity flexibility differentiates Aixtron from global
peers and improves production efficiency.

Valuation yet to reflect fundamentals. Our previous EW rating was framed
against a much higher P/E of 37x FY27 EPSe. The shares have pulled back 50%
since June peaks and now trade on 20x FY27 EPSe. This is a discount to both
optical and semi-cap peers as well as to its 5-year 1-Year Forward P/E average
(22x). Signs of a broadening recovery in power electronics, alongside durable
opto growth, now give us greater conviction that the stock should trade at a
premium to its historical average. As such we continue to apply a 25x P/E
multiple and move to OW. Applied to our higher FY27 EPSe €1.65, this sets our
PT at €42. We recognise that the macro environment and AI credit concerns
could weigh on sentiment, preventing stock outperformance. That said, with the
shares down 50% from June peaks and fundamentals strengthening, we see an
attractive entry point. We look next to Aixtron's FY26 results in March for
evidence that robust order intake converts into a FY27 sales guide ahead of
expectations. We move to OW, PT €42.

| Aixtron screens as attractive versus other optical peers.
 Source: Morgan Stanley
Research estimates (e)  
---  
We sit 6% ahead of consensus on FY27 Sales, 125bps on GM% and 135bps on OM%.
 Source: Visible Alpha
Consensus as of 29/10/26, Morgan Stanley Research estimates (e)  
---
